chapter.title: Listening Section
chapter.source: ETS — TOEFL iBT® Practice Test 1 (aligned with tests from January 21, 2026)

summary: Listening section of the official ETS Practice Test 1, in two modules. Module 1: Choose a Response (1–8), two conversations (9–12), an announcement (13–14) and a podcast talk (15–18). Module 2: Choose a Response (1–8), a conversation (9–10), an announcement (11–12) and an environmental science talk (13–16). The audio is the ETS recordings; transcripts are hidden until you reveal them. Answers come from the ETS answer keys (PDF pp. 25–26).

passage.title: Module 1 · Choose the best response
passage.text: Listen to each statement once, then pick the best reply. The statement is shown after you answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 1. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: As a matter of fact, I was returning a book.
Yes, you can find it in the reference section.
I don’t think I’ll have enough time to do that.
Actually, I think I can get there a little earlier.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: As a matter of fact, I was returning a book.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Didn’t I just see you in the library an hour ago?” — Answer key: (A) As a matter of fact, I was returning a book.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 2. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: I can help you find it.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: I can help you find it.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Where is the nearest bus stop?” — Answer key: (C) I can help you find it.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 3. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: Yes, you're allowed to do that.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Use the convenient chat feature.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “How do I contact customer service?” — Answer key: (B) Use the convenient chat feature.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 4. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: How about tomorrow night then?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “I'm afraid I'm not available this evening.” — Answer key: (B) How about tomorrow night then?

multiple_choice_questions.question: 5. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: I think he's come home already.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Let's check the schedule online.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Isn't the post office open today?” — Answer key: (D) Let's check the schedule online.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 6. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: I can help you with that.
You don't need any more information.
You have a lot of questions, don't you?
You haven't given me your number yet.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: You haven't given me your number yet.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “If you need me, just text.” — Answer key: (D) You haven't given me your number yet.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 7. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: Yes, there is a major power outage.
Yes, it's closed all day on Sunday.
Yes, they're having a huge sale.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Yes, they're having a huge sale.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “So the store is open for business all weekend?” — Answer key: (D) Yes, they're having a huge sale.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 8. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: I overslept.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Did you attend the seminar?” — Answer key: (A) I overslept.

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to a conversation
passage.transcript:
Woman: Need anything from the supermarket?
Man: Huh? Aren’t we getting ready to go see that play in a few minutes?
Woman: That’s tomorrow.
Man: Oh. Wow, I’d forget my head if it wasn’t screwed on…. Guess I don’t need to change my clothes after all.
Woman: So, you weren’t planning to prepare dinner?
Man: No, but I can. What do you want?
Woman: Just something light and healthy. So, can you go shopping instead?
Man: Yeah, sure. How about salmon and salad? Want anything else?
Woman: No, that’s good. Thanks!
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 9. What does the woman imply that she was about to do?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Go shopping
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) Go shopping

multiple_choice_questions.question: 10. Why does the man say “I’d forget my head if it wasn’t screwed on”?
choices: He forgot what the woman wanted him to buy.
He forgot about the timing of their plans.
He forgot what they were going to eat for dinner.
He forgot to buy salmon and salad at the supermarket.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: He forgot about the timing of their plans.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) He forgot about the timing of their plans.

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to a conversation
passage.transcript:
Man: Did you see the maintenance request about the air-conditioning?
Woman: Yes, I called the technician this morning. They said someone should be here shortly.
Man: That’s a relief. It’s getting uncomfortably warm in here.
Woman: I know—I called as soon as I noticed. Hopefully, it’s just a minor issue and they can get it working again without too much delay. In the meantime, why don’t you go out to lunch early? Maybe it’ll be better when you get back.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 11. Why did the woman call a technician?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: A room is too hot.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) A room is too hot.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 12. What does the woman suggest the man do?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Take a break early
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) Take a break early

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to an announcement in a classroom
passage.transcript: Man: Good afternoon, everyone. I am excited to inform you that Dr. Cynthia Palmer, a renowned expert in environmental science, will be giving a guest lecture next Monday at 2 PM in Waldman Auditorium. Dr. Palmer will discuss the latest advancements in sustainable energy solutions and their impact on global climate change. Due to her popularity and the high interest in her work, I highly recommend arriving early to secure a seat.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 13. What is the announcement about?
choices: A different location for a class
multiple_choice_questions.answer: A guest lecture
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) A guest lecture

multiple_choice_questions.question: 14. Why does the professor mention Dr. Palmer’s popularity?
choices: To encourage students to read her work
To indicate why she was invited to the university
To compare her to other invited experts
To explain why students should arrive early
multiple_choice_questions.answer: To explain why students should arrive early
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) To explain why students should arrive early

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to a talk on a podcast about psychology
passage.transcript:
Podcast Host: Did you see that new thriller movie that came out last week? I did and loved it. The action, the plot twists… I was totally captivated. Time just flew by. Not a single thought occurred to me that was unrelated to the movie. What I experienced is what psychologists call hard fascination. Hard fascination means intense focus and concentration. Whether it’s TV programs, video games... hard fascination is all too easy to come by in this modern world.

There’s another type of fascination—soft fascination. There’s still effortless attention, meaning that no special effort is required for you to stay focused, but there’s still room for other thoughts. When I take a walk in the park and look at the flowers and trees, for example, I might be thinking in the back of my mind about my dinner plans.

Now, one thing to know is hard fascination causes mental fatigue. The mind is so intensely focused that it gets tired fast. What follows mental fatigue? You might find yourself easily distracted, irritable, and stressed. Soft fascination, in contrast, engages a different part of the brain—the DMN, or Default Mode Network, which soothes the mind and helps combat mental fatigue. So next time you feel like your mind is on overload, turn off the TV, put down your phone. Take a walk, or simply sit and stare at the clouds.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 15. What is the topic of the talk?
choices: How to keep the mind focused
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Two types of fascination
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) Two types of fascination

multiple_choice_questions.question: 16. Why does the speaker mention a movie?
choices: To compare different types of movies
To introduce a concept in psychology
To explain how movies affect emotions
To encourage listeners to watch more movies
multiple_choice_questions.answer: To introduce a concept in psychology
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) To introduce a concept in psychology

multiple_choice_questions.question: 17. What does the speaker say about her walk in the park?
choices: It is similar to her experience watching a good movie.
Her mind has space for thoughts unrelated to nature.
She needs to put in special effort to stay focused on flowers and trees.
She gets mental fatigue from her mind engaging in hard fascination.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Her mind has space for thoughts unrelated to nature.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) Her mind has space for thoughts unrelated to nature.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 18. What does the speaker say about Default Mode Network?
choices: It is involved in soft fascination.
It leads to irritability and stress.
It is easily tired from overuse.
Its effect is unknown to psychologists.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: It is involved in soft fascination.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) It is involved in soft fascination.

passage.title: Module 2 · Choose the best response
passage.text: Listen to each statement once, then pick the best reply. The statement is shown after you answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 1. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: I’m unsure, but I can find out.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: I’m unsure, but I can find out.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Who is the new manager?” — Answer key: (B) I’m unsure, but I can find out.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 2. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: Please wait while I look that up.
No, I have another due date.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Please wait while I look that up.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “When is the due date for the report?” — Answer key: (A) Please wait while I look that up.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 3. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: The cinema is not open today.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Let’s go together.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “I’m going to get some groceries.” — Answer key: (D) Let’s go together.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 4. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: The break is in an hour.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: That would be great.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Would you like a copy of my notes?” — Answer key: (B) That would be great.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 5. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Should we join them?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Sami and Layla are on their way to the café.” — Answer key: (A) Should we join them?

multiple_choice_questions.question: 6. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: I’ll set up a meeting for us to talk.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: I’ll set up a meeting for us to talk.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “I'd like to hear your thoughts on the job candidates.” — Answer key: (B) I’ll set up a meeting for us to talk.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 7. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: We don't offer that.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “How much does expedited shipping cost?” — Answer key: (C) We don't offer that.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 8. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: What is her role in the company?
You ask a lot of questions.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: What is her role in the company?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “If you need more information, contact Ms. Lee.” — Answer key: (B) What is her role in the company?

passage.title: Module 2 · Listen to a conversation
passage.transcript:
Man: I’m trying to decide whether to get a smartphone or a tablet. What do you think?
Woman: It depends on what you need it for. If you want something portable and easy to use on the go, a smartphone is better.
Man: That’s true. But I like the larger screen on a tablet for watching videos and reading.
Woman: In that case....
Man: I better think about it some more.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 9. What is the man trying to decide between?
choices: A tablet and a desktop computer
multiple_choice_questions.answer: A smartphone and a tablet
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) A smartphone and a tablet

multiple_choice_questions.question: 10. What reason does the woman give for her suggestion?
choices: The device is easier to use on the go.
The device has a larger screen.
The device has better battery life.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: The device is easier to use on the go.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) The device is easier to use on the go.

passage.title: Module 2 · Listen to an announcement in a student lounge
passage.transcript: Man: Attention everyone! The student lounge will be closed tomorrow from one P.M. to three P.M. for maintenance. We will be repairing a broken pipe in the ceiling. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. Please plan accordingly and consider using the library or the campus café during this time.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 11. What is the main purpose of the announcement?
choices: To inform students about a schedule change
To notify students of a new facility
To encourage students to use the lounge more
multiple_choice_questions.answer: To inform students about a schedule change
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) To inform students about a schedule change

multiple_choice_questions.question: 12. What should students do during the closure?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Use alternate spaces
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) Use alternate spaces

passage.title: Module 2 · Listen to a talk in an environmental science class
passage.transcript:
Professor: An ecological footprint is a measure of the environmental impact of an individual, community, or country. It calculates the amount of natural resources consumed and the waste generated by human activities, usually expressed in global hectares. By comparing ecological footprints, we can understand how different lifestyles and practices contribute to resource depletion and environmental degradation.

For instance, the ecological footprint of someone living in a developed country is typically larger than that of someone living in a developing country, mainly due to higher consumption levels and waste production. Factors such as energy use, transportation, food consumption, and housing play significant roles in determining the size of an ecological footprint. Understanding ecological footprints is crucial for promoting sustainability. It helps identify areas where changes can be made to reduce environmental impact. For example, if you consume locally produced foods, you'll likely reduce your ecological footprint because less energy will be used for transporting that food. Governments and organizations can use ecological footprint data to develop policies aimed at achieving sustainable development. I'll discuss some examples of that next.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 13. What is the main topic of the talk?
choices: Changes in consumption in societies over time
The role of governments in sustainability
multiple_choice_questions.answer: A measure of environmental impact
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) A measure of environmental impact

multiple_choice_questions.question: 14. Why does the speaker mention developed and developing countries?
choices: To contradict a theory related to the ecological footprint
To show that resource depletion can be similar regardless of lifestyle
To illustrate the usefulness of comparing ecological footprints
To point out that production efficiency reduces the ecological footprint
multiple_choice_questions.answer: To illustrate the usefulness of comparing ecological footprints
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) To illustrate the usefulness of comparing ecological footprints

multiple_choice_questions.question: 15. What does the speaker mention as a way that people can reduce their ecological footprint?
choices: By using environmentally friendly forms of transportation
multiple_choice_questions.answer: By eating locally produced food
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) By eating locally produced food

multiple_choice_questions.question: 16. What will the speaker most likely discuss next?
choices: How information about ecological footprints has been used in creating policies
How data about ecological footprints has been collected
Why the idea of ecological footprint is often misunderstood
Why sustainable development can be difficult to achieve
multiple_choice_questions.answer: How information about ecological footprints has been used in creating policies
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) How information about ecological footprints has been used in creating policies
